summary: This bill permanently allows Medicare to pay federally qualified health centers and rural health clinics for telehealth services, including audio-only, and removes geographic restrictions for where patients can receive these services from such clinics.

scores.thoughts: This bill aims to make permanent the payment for telehealth services provided by federally qualified health centers and rural health clinics under Medicare, and removes originating site requirements. This expands access to healthcare services, particularly for those in rural areas, which aligns with expanding public healthcare access.

The bill permanently extends Medicare payments for telehealth services at FQHCs and RHCs (previously temporary), committing to ongoing federal spending without any offsetting revenue or cuts. This has a modest deficit-increasing effect but is not a central purpose of the legislation.

The core of the bill is a permanent expansion of Medicare telehealth coverage and reimbursement for FQHCs/RHCs, including audio-only services and removal of site restrictions, which constitutes direct government action to broaden access and lower barriers to care.
